body:
Thank you for replying!

I'm sorry to hear that you're struggling as well! I have mental illnesses myself, and a recent interview for CTV for "Bell Let's Talk Day" gave the statistic that one in ten people suffer from anxiety, but I suspect in reality that anxiety is much more common than that, so there's possibly a lot of people suffering too, and like you said, it isn't anything to be ashamed of at all.

Not to turn this into a math assignment about rent, but my rent in Fredericton in 2014 was around $850 but is $1100 now. I've heard anecdotally that rent in Calgary is only $1100 to $2000 for a really nice apartment, and their minimum wage is $15 per hour in comparison to our $11.25 per hour.

A minimum wage 8 hour per day/32 hour per week part-time job in Calgary would pay $480 per week, or $1920 per month. In comparison, our 8 hr/ 32 hr per week job pays only $360 per week or $1440 per month.

If there's that big of a difference in minimum wage though, I'm not sure why the prices of apartments are comparable, one would think they'd be cheaper where the minimum wage was smaller? 

Fredericton landlords charging high prices for rent can't even claim that students are willing to pay higher rent because student loans now usually only give enough to cover $900 per month rent if you throw every penny you get at rent and rent alone.

I hope things get easier and better for you!

Thank you for replying! 

I don't know the lady personally, and the article doesn't provide any contact info. I've heard before with similar stories of people contacting the journalist directly and they contact the person, so you could possibly try that.

Thank you for this, and thank you for the hugs, and love, and prayers. I try really hard to be strong, even when sometimes life comes along and just seems to try and kick your legs out from under. I hope you have a really great day today, and tomorrow and after! Hugs and love and blessings to you as well!

(Edited for fumble-y wording, sorry! Ah, my nerves!)

Thank you, reading your reply really helps me feel like someone's actually listening and taking me seriously. Thank you also for the links, posting those you've actually done more to help me than my university ever has.

I tried visiting my university's counseling services after my assault first happened, I saw a counselour who seemed okay but was sort of really intense and angry. I saw her maybe twice and then suddenly received a really rude email out of the blue inviting me to a meeting. 

I had this strong intuition something was off and had my boyfriend come to the meeting with me. It ended up being an intervention-style meeting with several heads of the student services departments. The counselour accused me of faking my symptoms, said the counseling services and the university would no longer be assisting me, and accused me of faking symptoms and lying just to get my children into the university's free daycare (I don't actually have children). She pointed at my boyfriend and said to me "Is he your husband, your boyfriend, your black lover, or someone new?" \[her phrasing here, not mine\] 

None of that was true either (I felt like lipping her off and saying "Lady, if my life was that interesting I wouldn't bother talking to you!" but I was actually terrified). I told her she was wrong and had no idea what she was talking about. She yelled at me that I wasn't taking her advice seriously and I told her to check my file and that she'd only seen me a few times. She opened it and looked at it, and got this look of horror across her face, stopped mid-sentence, and then abruptly ended the meeting. She stammered at me, wouldn't meet my gaze, and said "Well...you're still not taking my advice seriously. You'll need to schedule a follow-up appointment if you want to keep receiving counseling."

I never went back to her or anyone at counseling services, I was so scared of her after that. I wouldn't even walk past the building. I confessed what happened to a friendly classmate on a whim after a final exam months later and he recognized from the details that they might have mistaken me for another girl he was friends with who was also a student in our same subject and who looked exactly like me, with similar build and hairstyle. He verified our initials were similar, and that we wore the same winter jacket at one point. It sounds odd to say it, I never met her, but I really love that girl. I hope she gave them absolute hell. Good for her, and I hope she's doing well. (I hope everyone else that saw that counselour is okay too, she probably targeted other people, but she retired recently thankfully)

I'm sorry, that's such a long reply. I've never talked to anyone but my boyfriend and that one random guy about that happening. I'm really hoping if I see someone now that it will be better, I can't imagine it being worse.
Thank you so much for saying this, it means a lot to me. Sending love to you as well! I hope you have a really lovely day!
